title: Quantum Fisher information in a quenched $p + ip$ superfluid
abstract: The quantum Fisher information (QFI) is widely used to characterize quantum phases and transitions, but its diagnostic power sometimes relies on selecting special generators based on prior knowledge of the underlying physics. We ask whether this requirement can be relaxed in nonequilibrium systems by studying the QFI of the long-time asymptotic state of a two-dimensional p+ip superfluid following an instantaneous quench of the coupling strength, using the particle number within a large subextensive subsystem as the generator. In equilibrium, the ground-state QFI is continuous across the topological transition between the weak-pairing BCS and the strong-pairing BEC phases, showing no direct signature of the transition. After the quench, however, the QFI associated with the same generator distinguishes the three dynamical phases and can encode the topology of the pre-quench state. In phase I, with a vanishing order parameter, the QFI Fourier spectrum consists of a single zero-frequency spike determined by the nonequilibrium distribution function. In phase II, with a constant nonzero order parameter, the QFI spectrum contains a zero-frequency spike and two continua separated by a gap set by the minimum asymptotic quasiparticle energy. The continuum edge behavior reveals whether this minimum occurs at zero or finite momentum. In the former case, the spectral weight vanishes at the edge, with the sign just inside the continuum encoding the pre-quench topology for large subsystem. In phase III, with a time-periodic order parameter, the QFI spectrum exhibits discrete peaks at integer multiples of the oscillation frequency, together with continua associated with the Floquet quasienergy spectrum. Our results show that driving the system out of equilibrium can enhance the diagnostic power of the QFI for a standard physical observable, revealing information inaccessible in equilibrium.
summary: This paper investigates the diagnostic capability of the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) in a quenched p+ip superfluid. By analyzing the QFI spectrum after the quench, the authors show that the QFI can uniquely distinguish three distinct dynamical phases. This work highlights that non-equilibrium dynamics can reveal rich physical information inaccessible through equilibrium measurements.
main_problem: To determine if the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) retains its diagnostic power in non-equilibrium systems when using a simple, generic observable like particle number as the generator.
main_result: The QFI associated with the particle number distinguishes three distinct dynamical phases (I, II, and III) after a quench, revealing topological information inaccessible when the system is in equilibrium.
method: The QFI is calculated for the long-time asymptotic state following an instantaneous quench in a 2D p+ip superfluid, analyzing the resulting Fourier spectrum.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional p+ip superfluid, modeled using a BCS Hamiltonian framework, whose dynamics are studied after a quench of the coupling strength.

important_parameters: The quench process, the asymptotic quasiparticle energy gap, and the subsystem size $L_A$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large subsystem approximation ($L_A$) for initial spectral analysis, though results persist beyond this limit.
figures_summary: The notes reference Figure 1, which illustrates the three distinct dynamical phases (I, II, and III) characterized by the evolution of the order parameter.
paper_structure: The paper reviews QFI theory, presents results for the equilibrium state (showing no transition signature), and then details the distinct spectral signatures found in the three non-equilibrium dynamical phases (I, II, and III).
why_interesting: It demonstrates that non-equilibrium dynamics can enhance the diagnostic power of quantum information measures like QFI, providing new tools to probe quantum phases beyond equilibrium thermodynamics.
